newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tabloid stops trailing Kennedy honeymooners.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tabloid stops trailing Kennedy honeymooners.

text.p: The world's most watched newlyweds had moved their honeymoon from Turkey to the Greek islands by Monday, but at least one U.S. tabloid said it had dropped off the trail of John F. Kennedy Jr and his bride.

The Globe, which broke the story last week that Kennedy and Carolyn Bessette were honeymooning in Turkey, said it would stop following the couple after taking "exclusive" pictures that were published in its latest issue.
"John Kennedy personally asked our news team to allow him to enjoy his honeymoon," said Tony Frost, editor of Boca Raton, Fla.-based Globe. "And I am delighted to honour his request."
Kennedy, often called the world's most eligible bachelor, married Bessette secretly on Sept. 21 on a small island off the coast of Georgia.
Although the couple managed to elude the world press and hold a private ceremony, a team of Globe journalists found them in Istanbul.
The tabloid published photos of their honeymoon in its latest issue, which hit newsstands last weekend.

Frost said his crew followed the honeymooners from Istanbul to the Turkish city of Izmir last Thursday and photographed them having breakfast at a roadside cafe. There, Kennedy approached the Globe team and politely said: "I hope you aren't going to follow us everywhere."
Frost said the conversation led him to decide to end the pursuit.
The New York Daily News said in Monday's editions that the couple, wearing dark glasses and travelling as "Mr. and Mrs. Hyannis," had left Turkey and were in the Greek islands by Monday.
"My understanding is that that's the case," Frost said, adding that he did not want to go further because he had agreed to stop following the couple.
